title: introduce-seq-checksum-framing-to-harden-mid-json-delimiter-glitch
author: Evan Park
description: Motivation: intermittent client-visible partial JSON payloads were observed during high-concurrency streaming sessions when a delimiter boundary and UTF-8 token split coincide, causing downstream OpenAI-compatible parsers to error or drop tool/function call sentinels. This PR introduces a lightweight sequence+checksum framing field appended to SSE payload metadata which enables deterministic reassembly and quick corruption detection without changing the public HTTP/SSE wire shape or requiring clients to update parsers. Changes include: 1) append a 6-byte ascii-safe seq-checksum token to internal streaming events when compatibility mode is active; 2) framer/resynchronizer logic that uses the checksum to identify mid-JSON delimiter splits and perform bounded replay/reslice of buffered fragments; 3) heuristics to fallback to legacy heuristics if framing metadata is absent (preserves interop with older servers/clients); 4) end-to-end fuzz tests exercising UTF-8 utf-8-split, delimiter-adjacent tokenization and toolcall boundary cases; 5) minimal perf regression mitigations (batch path early-exit, checksum table caching). This is implemented in the OpenAI compatibility layer only and has no API surface changes. Rollout plan: staged rollout behind a feature flag, enable for 10% of traffic for two days, expand to 100% if no error increase, short-circuit flag for emergency rollback. Related: ENG-1342 (stability sampling), SUP-4421 (customer incident #4321). Checklist: - [x] design doc linked in PR comments - [x] unit + integration tests - [x] fuzz harness added - [x] benchmark smoke to validate <2% p95 token latency regression - [x] feature flag gating and rollout plan documented

implement framer resync and bounded replay (stream_framer.go)

review_comments: Maya Singh: Can you justify the 6-byte token length? We should quantify collision rate and how it affects replay windows.
Evan Park: 6 bytes == 48 bits of entropy when interpreted on encode path; with our window size 10k events the collision probability is <1e-9. Added rationale and table to docs/compatibility.md.
Rahul Gupta: Please add a targeted benchmark showing the p95 token latency impact on 4k context with batching enabled.
Evan Park: Added microbenchmark and optimized table lookup; p95 regression observed at +0.9% in our smoke runs and is documented in benchmarks.md.
Clara Johns: Ensure the fallback path is explicitly instrumented so we can alert if an older client is causing excessive fallbacks.
Evan Park: Added a metric (compat.fallback.count) and an alert rule in observability pack.
release_notes: Fixes intermittent partial-JSON errors during SSE streaming by adding an optional seq+checksum framing token in the OpenAI compatibility layer. Backwards-compatible and gated behind a feature flag.
